topicWeightsNote: Official documents give only section totals. Topic weights inside a section are a project assumption used to spread coverage; they are not an official distribution and should be replaced by previous-year paper analysis when verified papers are imported.

topics.name: Indian History and Freedom Movement
topics.conceptNote: Focus on landmark events, dynasties and leaders: Indus Valley, Mauryas and Guptas, the Delhi Sultanate and Mughals, the 1857 revolt, and the national movement (INC 1885, Non-Cooperation 1920, Civil Disobedience 1930, Quit India 1942). Learn the year, the leader and the outcome together.

topics.name: Indian Geography
topics.conceptNote: Know the major rivers and where they rise, the states and capitals, mountain ranges, soils and the main crops. Rivers that flow west into the Arabian Sea (Narmada, Tapti) are a frequent trap.

topics.name: Indian Constitution and Polity
topics.conceptNote: Remember key articles (Art. 21 life and liberty, Art. 32 constitutional remedies, Art. 356 President's rule), the structure of Parliament (Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha), who appoints whom, and fundamental rights versus directive principles.

topics.name: Indian Economy
topics.conceptNote: Know what RBI, NITI Aayog and GST are, the meaning of GDP and inflation, and major welfare schemes. Definitions are tested more than numbers.

topics.name: Madhya Pradesh General Knowledge
topics.conceptNote: Madhya Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 with Bhopal as its capital. Learn its rivers (Narmada rises at Amarkantak), national parks (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench), UNESCO sites (Khajuraho, Sanchi, Bhimbetka), tribes (Gond, Bhil, Baiga) and folk culture.

subtopics.name: MP History, Heritage and Culture
subtopics.nameHi: मध्यप्रदेश का इतिहास, धरोहर एवं संस्कृति

topics.name: Static GK, Sports and Awards
topics.nameHi: स्थैतिक सामान्य ज्ञान, खेल एवं पुरस्कार
topics.conceptNote: Books and authors, national symbols, sports terms, international organisations and their headquarters. Learn in pairs (book–author, organisation–headquarters).

topics.name: Basic Computer Knowledge
topics.conceptNote: Know input and output devices, memory types (RAM is volatile, ROM is not), units (1 KB = 1024 bytes), common shortcuts and basic internet terms.

topics.name: Coding–Decoding
topics.conceptNote: Write the alphabet with positions (A=1 … Z=26). Find the rule from the example (shift each letter by +n, reverse, or position sums) and apply exactly the same rule to the new word. Check the rule on every letter, not just the first.

topics.name: Alphabet Series
topics.conceptNote: Convert letters to positions, find the gap pattern (constant, increasing, alternating), then convert back. Remember that the alphabet wraps after Z only if the question says so.

topics.name: Blood Relations
topics.conceptNote: Draw a family tree: generations vertically, spouses horizontally, + for male and − for female. Resolve the statement one relation at a time from the end.

topics.name: Direction Sense
topics.conceptNote: Draw the path with north up. Right turn from North faces East; left turn from North faces West. Final distance from the start uses Pythagoras when the net movement is along two axes.

topics.name: Analogy and Classification
topics.conceptNote: State the relationship of the first pair in a sentence ("a pen is used to write"), then test each option with the same sentence. For odd-one-out, find the property shared by three options.

topics.name: Number Series
topics.conceptNote: Look at the differences between terms first, then the second differences, then ratios. Common patterns: constant difference, increasing difference, ×n, squares and cubes, and alternating patterns.

topics.name: Number System, LCM and HCF
topics.conceptNote: HCF is the largest number dividing all given numbers; LCM is the smallest number divisible by all of them. For two numbers, HCF × LCM = product. Use prime factorisation: HCF takes the lowest powers, LCM the highest.

topics.name: Simplification (BODMAS)
topics.conceptNote: Apply BODMAS strictly: Brackets, Orders, Division and Multiplication left to right, then Addition and Subtraction left to right. Most errors come from adding before multiplying.

topics.name: Order and Ranking
topics.conceptNote: Total = position from top + position from bottom − 1. Position from the other end = total − position + 1.

topics.name: Calendar and Clock
topics.conceptNote: Clock: angle = |30H − 5.5M| degrees. Calendar: an ordinary year shifts the weekday by 1, a leap year by 2; count odd days modulo 7.

topics.name: Problems on Ages
topics.conceptNote: Let the present ages be variables, then move every statement to the same time point. The difference between two people's ages never changes.

topics.name: Physics in Everyday Life
topics.conceptNote: Know SI units (force: newton, work and energy: joule, power: watt, current: ampere), Newton's laws, speed of light and sound, reflection and refraction, and simple electric circuits.

topics.name: Chemistry in Everyday Life
topics.conceptNote: Know common chemical formulas (water H2O, common salt NaCl, baking soda NaHCO3), acids and bases (pH below 7 is acidic), metals and non-metals, and everyday reactions such as rusting.

topics.name: Biology, Health and Environment
topics.conceptNote: Know the human organ systems, vitamins and the diseases caused by their deficiency (vitamin C – scurvy, vitamin D – rickets), photosynthesis, and basic ecology (food chains, pollution).

topics.name: Percentage
topics.conceptNote: x% of N = N × x / 100. Percentage change = (change ÷ original) × 100. Successive changes of a% and b% give a net change of a + b + ab/100 percent, not a + b.

topics.name: Profit and Loss
topics.conceptNote: Profit % and loss % are always calculated on the cost price, not the selling price. SP = CP × (100 + P%) / 100. Discount is calculated on the marked price.

subtopics.name: Cost Price, Selling Price and Discount
subtopics.nameHi: क्रय मूल्य, विक्रय मूल्य एवं छूट

topics.name: Ratio and Proportion
topics.conceptNote: To divide N in the ratio a : b, the parts are N × a/(a+b) and N × b/(a+b). Add the ratio parts first, then multiply.

topics.name: Average
topics.conceptNote: Average = sum ÷ count. When one value is added or removed, find the new sum first: new sum = old average × old count ± value.

topics.name: Simple and Compound Interest
topics.conceptNote: Simple interest = P × R × T / 100. Compound amount = P × (1 + R/100)^T. Compound interest = amount − principal. Over 2 years, CI − SI = P × (R/100)².

topics.name: Time and Work
topics.conceptNote: If A finishes a job in a days, A does 1/a of it per day. Working together, rates add: 1/a + 1/b. Time together = ab / (a + b).

topics.name: Time, Speed and Distance
topics.conceptNote: Distance = speed × time. Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18. Average speed for equal distances is 2xy/(x + y), not the simple average.

topics.name: Mensuration
topics.conceptNote: Rectangle area = l × b and perimeter = 2(l + b). Circle area = πr² and circumference = 2πr. Use π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7.
